grid_vs_metric.hazard: Running the sim in projected national-grid coordinates instead of a true metric frame distorts distances or speeds enough to matter over a 4 km site.

los_sampling.hazard: Line of sight sampled every 2 m against a 4 m terrain mesh will miss thin obstacles or ridge crests and report false visibility.

no_vegetation.hazard: Ignoring forest canopy in line of sight makes detection ranges in wooded terrain unrealistically optimistic.

osm_graph_gaps.hazard: The OSM path graph has disconnected components or missing links, so routing fails or agents take absurd detours.

float_replay.hazard: Floating-point math in routing or line of sight breaks bit-identical replay across machines or library versions.

rng_coupling.hazard: Adding or removing one agent changes the random numbers other agents receive, making runs incomparable.

dwell_determinism.hazard: A purely geometric dwell-time detection model overstates how reliably human guards and cameras detect people.

interrupt_teleport.hazard: Re-tasking an agent in the middle of a leg causes a position jump or a speed-limit violation.

drone_cliff.hazard: A straight-line terrain-following drone path over 300 m cliffs demands impossible climb rates or clips terrain.

quiet_skip.hazard: Skipping sensing while no drill subject is present hides events that should have happened, so long-horizon results differ from full stepping.

off_road.hazard: Restricting people and robot dogs to mapped paths misrepresents intruders, who would move cross-country.

dual_use.hazard: A simulator that scores guard detection and response at a site could be used to plan how to evade guards at a real facility.
